Check and Add Package Prefixes to Function Calls

Source: R/colons_check.R
colons_check.Rd

Checks that the functions called inside a function are preceded by their package (e.g., base::mean() and not mean()), and adds the missing <package>:: prefixes before the basic R functions (functions of the base, stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets and methods packages).

Usage

colons_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Function to check, written without quotes and brackets (e.g., fun1 or pkg::fun1).

export

Single logical value. If TRUE, the corrected function is written into the <name>_safer.R file of out_path instead of being returned (e.g., fun1_safer.R for x = fun1 or x = pkg::fun1), as fun1_safer <- function(...), which base::source() recreates. Nothing is written if nothing has to be corrected, but an error is returned if the file already exists, or if x is not a function name (e.g., function(x){x} or FUN_LIST$fun).

out_path

Single character string: path of an existing folder where the file is written. Required when export is TRUE; otherwise not used, but a non-NULL value must still be a single non-empty character string. NULL by default.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

The corrected function, which keeps the environment of x: x with the <package>:: prefixes added before its calls of basic R functions.

NULL, invisibly, if nothing has to be corrected, if x contains no function call, as a primitive function like base::sum (with a warning), or if export is TRUE.

In addition, except when x contains no function call, a report is printed with message(): either a message saying that everything seems clean, or tables of the calls without prefix, one for the basic R functions and one for the other functions (column 1: line number; column 2: function name; column 3: code before the function name). The internal functions called (see the Details section) are then also listed.

Details

A call of a basic R function gets the prefix of its package (e.g., mean() becomes base::mean()) only if the function found by R when running x, from the environment of x (functions defined by the user, imported functions and attached packages), is this basic function. Otherwise, the name is masked (e.g., filter() with the dplyr package attached, or a filter() function defined in the global environment): the call is not modified and is reported with the other functions. Under pkgload::load_all() (devtools::load_all()), system.file(), help(), library.dynam() and library.dynam.unload() can thus be reported as masked by the pkgload shims. In code evaluated in another environment (e.g., expr of with(), or .() of bquote() with where), a function of that environment named like a basic function is not detected: its calls get the basic prefix. The stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets and methods packages must be attached, as in a default R session, otherwise an error is returned.

The calls of internal functions, written without :: or :::, are not modified, nor reported as missing a prefix. The internal functions are the functions created inside x (names assigned a function definition or a utils::getFromNamespace() result), the arguments of x and of all the functions defined in x, anonymous ones included (e.g., FUN in FUN(y)), but not the arguments and local functions of those written in quoted code (e.g., c in bquote(function(c) .(c(y)))), and x itself when written as a name, like fun1 or pkg::fun1 (recursive calls). These names are recognized in the function that defines them (the whole code of x for its arguments, x itself and <<-): an argument t of a function defined in x does not prevent the check of t() outside this function. A name assigned another value is not an internal function: after c <- 3, c(y) calls base::c() and gets its prefix. A local name that holds a function obtained otherwise is not detected: after rev <- base::get(x = "sort"), rev(y) becomes base::rev(y).

The calls of the other functions are reported in the message and in a warning, but not modified, because their package cannot be determined reliably: add their prefixes manually.

Not checked: function names written between quotes (like "+"()), preceded by $ or @, or written without brackets (like as.character in sapply(1:3, FUN = as.character)), and function, if, for, while, repeat and else. Neither are the calls inside formulas, including the one-sided formulas used as lambdas (e.g., log() and offset() in y ~ log(x) + offset(z), or mean() in ~ mean(.x)), because modeling functions use their text, the calls inside quote(), bquote(), expression(), alist() and substitute(), whose arguments are code used as data (e.g., paste() in the plotmath label expression(paste("Temp (", degree, "C)"))), except the code that R evaluates (.() and spliced ..() of bquote(), its where argument, and the env argument of substitute()), nor the function called by .Internal() (e.g., toupper in .Internal(toupper(x))). The other functions that use the code of their arguments get the corrected code (e.g., the default axis label of ggplot2::aes(x = log(y)) becomes base::log(y)). Comments are not checked, but some unexpected writing could dupe colons_check(): please report it here.

Names already preceded by :: or ::: are not checked (R CMD check reports the wrong ones, e.g., base:::sum() or base::dev.off()). The added prefixes are always ::.

Source references: line 1 is the line of the function keyword. Comments and indentation are kept only if x carries its source references (attribute srcref). Functions created with options(keep.source = FALSE) (default of Rscript) and functions of installed packages (e.g., saferDev::colons_check) have none: their deparsed code is analyzed, without comments and with line numbers that differ from the source file.

If the corrected code does not parse (a writing that the analysis does not handle, e.g., a function name at the beginning of a line, after a $ or @ ending the previous line), x is returned unchanged with a warning, or an error is returned if export is TRUE.

An error is returned if x contains \(x) lambda functions (only detected with source references): run lambda_check() first.

See also

The code checkers of saferDev, in the recommended order of use: super_assign_check, lambda_check, colons_check, all_args_here, curly_bracket_check, true_false_check, for_loop_nb_check (see vignette("saferDev")).

Examples

# Without source references ("Run examples" link, Rscript), line numbers and comments differ.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/colons_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){
    y <- mean(x) # mean() written without base::
    base::return(y)
}
fun1_safer <- saferDev::colons_check(x = fun1, export = FALSE, out_path = NULL,
    safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # base:: added before mean()
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS:
#> 
#> LINE	FUN		STRING_BEFORE
#> 3	mean		y <- 
#> 
fun1_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     y <- base::mean(x)
#>     base::return(y)
#> }
#> <environment: 0x6235c3377f88>
# Write the corrected function in the fun1_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(check = FALSE),
    fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::colons_check(x = fun1, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS:
#> 
#> LINE	FUN		STRING_BEFORE
#> 3	mean		y <- 
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpQNRq2A/dir1104737e2dfc/fun1_safer.R
#> 
base::unlink(x = tempo_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = FALSE, expand = TRUE) # folder removed
